proof_summary: Direct calculation checks the required expansions for \(43\) and exhibits a base with three distinct digits for every \(44\le k\le399\). For \(k\ge400\), write \(k=n^2+x\) with \(n=\lfloor\sqrt{k}\rfloor\) and \(0\le x\le2n\); a case split on \(x\) chooses a base among \(n,n-1,n-2,n-3\) in which \(k\) has three pairwise distinct digits.
